steps.label: P: solvable quickly
steps.sub: Polynomial time, O(n), O(n²), O(n⁵) — sorting, primality testing, shortest path

steps.label: NP: verifiable quickly
steps.sub: Not "slow to solve" — a candidate certificate can be checked in polynomial time

steps.label: NP-complete: the hardest problems in NP
steps.sub: SAT, TSP-decision, graph coloring — no polynomial-time algorithm known for any

steps.label: P ⊆ NP ⊆ PSPACE ⊆ EXPTIME
steps.sub: The proven containment chain; whether P = NP remains unsolved

caption: At just n=100, O(2^n) already exceeds the atoms in a small planet — exponential time is a wall, not just "slow."

steps.label: PSPACE: bounded by memory, not time
steps.sub: Game-tree evaluation reuses space while backtracking, even over exponentially many nodes

steps.label: EXPTIME: time grows like O(2^n)
steps.sub: No restriction on memory at all

steps.label: The chain is proven; strictness isn't
steps.sub: Nobody has shown any of these containments is strict everywhere

steps.label: This table is the baseline for the whole course
steps.sub: Every later quantum-speedup claim gets measured against it

subtitle: Where quantum computers' own complexity class fits against this classical baseline.
